literal: Good natured you are, may you live, O Anicha flower! Than you, of softer nature is she whom I love.
translation: May you live long, O Anicha flower, for you are indeed of a delicate nature! Yet, she whom I love is of an even softer nature than you.
modern: அனிச்சப் பூவே! நீ நல்ல மென்மையான இயல்பைக் கொண்டிருக்கிறாய், நீ வாழ்க! ஆனால், நான் விரும்பும் என் காதலி உன்னை விடவும் மென்மையான இயல்புடையவள் ஆவாள்.
explanation: The poet addresses the delicate Anicha flower, which is famous in classical Tamil literature for being so sensitive that it withers merely upon being smelled. He praises the flower's gentle nature and wishes it well. However, he immediately elevates his beloved above the flower, declaring that she whom he loves possesses a nature that is even softer and more delicate than the flower itself. This comparison beautifully highlights the supreme tenderness and grace of the beloved.
